lessons.title: Check DFA fluctuation scaling
objectives: Separate the fluctuation curve from its fitted scaling exponent.
Verify amplitude and offset invariants through the public Python API.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Analyze the fixed signal at the four explicit scales.
Analyze three times the signal plus seven.
Compare fluctuations and alpha without claiming that this signal proves long-range dependence.

starter.code:
import numpy as np
from opentsx import DFA
values = np.sin(np.arange(256) * 0.37) + 0.2 * np.cos(np.arange(256) * 0.13)
scales = np.array([8, 16, 32, 64], dtype=np.int32)
result = DFA(polynom_order=1).analyze(values, scales=scales)
changed = DFA(polynom_order=1).analyze(3 * values + 7, scales=scales)

expected: Both results preserve scales [8,16,32,64].
Changed fluctuations equal three times the original within 1e-12 relative and absolute tolerance.
The fitted exponent stays equal within 1e-12; the input array remains unchanged.
pitfalls: A short synthetic signal is a test fixture, not evidence of a physical scaling law.

lessons.title: Select explicit MFDFA moments
objectives: Relate the q=2 fluctuation row to DFA.
Interpret moment indices using q_values.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Analyze the same signal with q values [-2,0,2].
Find q=2 explicitly and compare its Fq row with DFA fluctuations.
Inspect the mass exponent at q=0.

starter.code:
import numpy as np
from opentsx import DFA
values = np.sin(np.arange(256) * 0.37) + 0.2 * np.cos(np.arange(256) * 0.13)
scales = np.array([8, 16, 32, 64], dtype=np.int32)
from opentsx import MFDFA
q_values = np.array([-2.0, 0.0, 2.0])
result = MFDFA(polynom_order=1, q_range=q_values).analyze(values, scales=scales)
q2 = int(np.flatnonzero(result["q_values"] == 2)[0])
fluctuations_q2 = result["Fq"][q2]

expected: Fq has shape (3,4) and contains finite values for this fixture.
The selected q=2 row equals DFA fluctuations within 1e-12.
tau_q at the q=0 index is -1.
pitfalls: The current h_2 convenience field selects the middle array element; use explicit q_values/h_q indices for custom q ranges.

lessons.title: Explain directional event synchronization
objectives: Identify planted events and their lead direction.
Distinguish a strict lag cap from an inclusive threshold.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Plant four spikes in each series with B one tick after A.
Analyze with tau_max two, then one.
Compare directional synchronization and the reported leader.

starter.code:
import numpy as np
from opentsx import EventSynchronization
first = np.zeros(25)
second = np.zeros(25)
first[[2,8,14,20]] = 10
second[[3,9,15,21]] = 10
result = EventSynchronization(tau_max=2).analyze(first, second, threshold1=5, threshold2=5)
capped = EventSynchronization(tau_max=1).analyze(first, second, threshold1=5, threshold2=5)

expected: Cap two gives overall_sync=1, sync_1_to_2=1, sync_2_to_1=0 and leader Series 1.
Cap one gives overall_sync=0 because the lag must be strictly below the cap.
pitfalls: Event synchronization is not Pearson correlation.
Use a fixed seed when adding surrogate_sync; a reproducible surrogate does not establish causality.

lessons.title: Measure exact return intervals
objectives: Derive return intervals from event indices.
Distinguish empirical survival from a fitted tail law.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Plant events at indices 1,3,7,13 in fifteen samples.
Analyze with a fixed absolute threshold of five.
Compute empirical survival and explain the absence of a qualified tail fit.

starter.code:
import numpy as np
from opentsx import RIS
values = np.zeros(15)
values[[1,3,7,13]] = 10
ris = RIS(threshold=5)
result = ris.analyze(values)
intervals, survival = ris.survival_function(result["return_intervals"])

expected: Return intervals are [2,4,6], with mean and median four.
Empirical survival is [1,2/3,1/3] at those intervals.
Three intervals leave gamma and tau_0 at zero in this implementation.
pitfalls: Intervals are in sample positions unless the sample period supplies a time unit.
Zero fit parameters for this short fixture are not a measured physical tail exponent.

lessons.title: Normalize retrieval inputs with gaps
objectives: Use population-standard-deviation scaling for retrieval.
Observe the normalized representation of flat input and NaNs.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Normalize [1,2,3,NaN].
Normalize a constant [7,7] array.
Compare this population scale with the sample scale of the UI normalization lesson.
expected: Normalized values are [-sqrt(1.5),0,sqrt(1.5),0] within 1e-12.
Constant input becomes [0,0].
pitfalls: A NaN becomes zero in this normalized representation; do not infer that raw missing data was observed as zero.

lessons.title: Weight fractional PAA boundaries
objectives: Reduce an array without requiring its length to divide the target width.
Account for fractional boundary weights.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Reduce [0,2,4,6,8] to width two.
Explain the half-weight of the middle value in each segment.
Try an empty input and identify the boundary rejection.

starter.code:
import org.opentsx.retrieval.pattern.Paa;
var reduced = Paa.of(new double[]{0,2,4,6,8}, 2);

expected: The reduced values are [1.6,6.4] within 1e-12.
Empty input rejects with IllegalArgumentException.
pitfalls: Skipping NaNs changes each segment's effective weight.
Choose width no larger than the input for this reduction exercise.

lessons.title: Encode comparable SAX words
objectives: Compose normalization, PAA and breakpoint encoding.
Preserve the width/alphabet identity of stored words.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Normalize [1,2,3,4] and encode width two/alphabet four.
Repeat after an affine value transformation.
Measure the same word against itself and reject alphabet one.
expected: The stored word is 2x4:ad; its distance lower bound to itself is zero.
Normalized [12,14,16,18] gives the same word.
Alphabet one rejects; supported alphabet sizes are 2 through 26.
pitfalls: Sax.word expects already normalized values.
A pruning lower bound is not an exact final similarity score.

lessons.title: Find a shape while excluding gaps
objectives: Interpret a distance profile as candidate start positions.
Distinguish invalid windows from poor finite matches.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Search [1,2,1,0] inside the supplied nine-sample array.
Identify which windows contain NaN.
Locate both identical shapes.

starter.code:
import org.opentsx.retrieval.pattern.Mass;
var profile = Mass.distanceProfile(new double[]{1,2,1,0}, new double[]{1,2,1,0,Double.NaN,1,2,1,0});

expected: The profile length is six.
Positions zero and five have distance zero within 1e-6.
Positions one through four have positive-infinity distance.
pitfalls: MASS computes normalized Euclidean distances, not raw amplitude error.
Do not interpret positive infinity as an ordinary numeric score.

lessons.title: Control time warping with a band
objectives: Compare diagonal-only matching with permitted time stretching.
Separate sample-count bands from search-config fractions.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Compare [0,1,1,0] with [0,0,1,0] using bands zero and one.
Reject a Distance.dtw fraction above one.
Explain why normalized search performs a normalization step separately.
expected: Diagonal-only distance is one; band one permits a zero-distance alignment.
Distance.dtw(1.1) rejects.
pitfalls: The direct Dtw band is an integer number of positions; Distance.dtw uses a fraction in [0,1].
This direct method does not automatically normalize the arrays.

lessons.title: Map a cross-episode search hit
objectives: Assemble contiguous per-series runs.
Map a match back to its starting episode and offset.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Build adjacent episodes [9,1,2] and [1,0,9] at one-second spacing.
Search for [1,2,1,0] with topK one.
Inspect the returned starting episode, offset and length.
expected: One match starts in episode first at offset one and has length four.
Its distance is zero within 1e-6 although the match crosses an episode boundary.
pitfalls: Queries need at least four finite values.
A time gap splits a run; non-overlapping top-k results need not include every candidate window.

lessons.title: Cut epoch-aligned duration windows
objectives: Explain epoch alignment and the bounded final partial window.
Retain strategy and time-axis metadata.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Build seven one-second samples [0,1,2,3,4,5,6].
Segment into four-second windows.
Inspect each segment's start and sample count.
expected: Output values are [0,1,2,3] and [4,5,6].
The second segment starts at 4000000 epoch microseconds.
pitfalls: Duration windows flush a partial tail; fixed-count windows use a different tail policy.

lessons.title: Overlap complete sample-count windows
objectives: Calculate step size from count and overlap.
Observe the dropped incomplete tail.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Segment the same seven values with count four and overlap two.
Identify the two shared sample positions.
Reject overlap equal to the count.
expected: Output values are [0,1,2,3] and [2,3,4,5].
The incomplete window starting at sample four is dropped.
Segmenter.fixedCount(4,4) rejects.
pitfalls: Overlap duplicates samples across output episodes intentionally; it is not source replay.

lessons.title: Retain a finalized peak neighbourhood
objectives: Separate prominence, peak separation and output extent.
Identify the anchor independently of segment start.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Segment [0,0,1,4,1,0,0,0] with the stated parameters.
Inspect the three-sample output and anchor.
Explain why a streaming detector needs lookahead.
expected: One segment contains [1,4,1].
Its anchor is 3000000 epoch microseconds; pre/post endpoints are inclusive.
pitfalls: A high current sample is not a finalized local maximum.
Prominence is measured against surrounding minima, not the global series mean.

lessons.title: Carry hysteresis state across episodes
objectives: Retain a phase across an input block boundary.
Distinguish the entry anchor from pre/post context.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Build [0,0,5] and adjacent [5,2,0,0,0] episodes.
Use ABOVE, enter four, exit three, pre/post one second and zero duration limits.
Compare StreamingSegmenter output plus flush with Segmentations.segment.
expected: One segment contains [0,5,5,2], anchored at 2000000 epoch microseconds.
Incremental and bounded results are exactly equal for the same source episodes.
pitfalls: For ABOVE, exit cannot exceed enter.
Zero maxDuration means unlimited, not zero-length output.

lessons.title: Close event-time statistics windows
objectives: Compute bounded window and global statistics through the public engine.
Distinguish missing samples from duplicate episode replay.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Configure a four-second window and a one-second expected interval.
Submit [1,2,NaN,3], then submit the same episode again.
Inspect window counts/mean and global emission; explain which samples entered the statistics.
expected: The closed window has three valid values, one NaN and mean two.
Submitting the same episode ID again adds no values and returns no new windows.
A repeated unchanged emitGlobal call returns no additional statistics.
pitfalls: Floating-point merges are not bitwise associative.
DDSketch relative-error claims exclude its zero bucket and collapsed tails unless separately qualified.
Duplicate suppression covers only episode IDs retained within Config.dedupCapacity; an evicted ID can be counted again.
The three-argument TsxStatsWindow constructor keeps incremental state without final flushing; bounded() flushes and includes changed GLOBAL, while window() flushes then selects its explicit windows.

lessons.title: Judge statistics against explicit expectations
objectives: Separate completeness and plausible-range checks.
Use a fixed clock for freshness.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Summarize the same [1,2,NaN,3] four-second episode.
Evaluate a plausible range [0,10] and one-second expected sampling.
Explain why completeness fails while plausible range passes, without treating the source as an operating fault.
expected: Completeness is 0.75 and fails the default 0.95 threshold.
The values remain within [0,10], so plausible range succeeds.
With last sample at three seconds and now at six, freshness fails the two-second age limit.
pitfalls: Freshness is evaluated only when maxAge and explicit nowMicros are supplied.
A constant legitimate operating state is not automatically a faulty sensor; choose flatline policy for the signal.

lessons.title: Preserve records through Avro single-object encoding
objectives: Inspect the wire envelope and decode the exact record type.
Separate schema fingerprint compatibility from arbitrary decoding.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Build a regular episode with a fixed ID and clock.
Encode and decode it as Episode.
Compare one existing shared wire-vector hex value and inspect its fingerprint.
expected: The decoded episode equals the original, including time axis and provenance.
Shared wire vectors require identical hex, not only equivalent values.
The default frame begins with bytes c3 01 and its eight-byte schema fingerprint.
pitfalls: Unknown writer schemas require explicit registration or a resolver.
A Confluent frame and an Avro single-object frame have different headers.

lessons.title: Construct one whole-topic source fragment
objectives: Separate logical source construction from broker execution.
Represent all internal ranges of a whole-topic assignment.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Construct a read description for both partitions of one synthetic topic.
Compute the Episode fingerprint from the registered schema.
Inspect source.read without opening a broker; use the existing wire/settings tests for offline evidence.
expected: Source metadata describes one topic with internal ranges for partitions zero and one.
Construction alone performs no reads.
Wire tests preserve allowed record bytes and settings tests prohibit group commits.
pitfalls: Partition positions are checkpoint/cut metadata, never independently deployable units.
The current source materializes an increment in memory; broker integration is a separate disposable-environment check.

lessons.title: Construct an acknowledged topic sink
objectives: Connect a source and sink in a logical Wayang plan.
Distinguish offline wire/settings checks from actual publication.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Construct a sink for a synthetic output topic.
Inspect its binding and connect an existing logical source using connectTo(0,sink,0).
Explain why acknowledgements and deterministic records do not make the transport exactly once.
expected: The sink names tsx.learning.clean.v2 and construction performs no writes.
Existing tests require no idempotence, acks=all and one request in flight.
Wire conversion preserves the encoded record bytes; actual delivery requires a separate broker test.
pitfalls: Do not point a learning exercise at production topics.
A sink object or successful wire encoding is not evidence that a record was published.

lessons.title: Round-trip local increment positions
objectives: Persist next positions for every internal partition of one topic.
Observe actual absence, mismatch and corruption behavior.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Write a checkpoint with next offsets ten and seven for one whole topic.
Load with the matching hash, then a different hash.
Use the existing corruption regression to distinguish an unreadable file from absence.
expected: Matching load returns next positions {0:10,1:7}.
Absence and a different specHash return an empty Optional in this local API.
Unreadable existing JSON raises IllegalStateException instead of being silently ignored.
The sixth constructor argument is the per-node operator-state map; this starter uses an empty map, while the checkpoint regression preserves nonempty state.
pitfalls: Current hash-mismatch behavior is not the proposed fail-closed orchestration state-ABI policy.
A local checkpoint provides neither distributed ownership nor exactly-once output.

lessons.title: Reject split-topic physical assignments offline
objectives: Keep the smallest deployable unit at a whole topic.
Preserve exact source/fragment identities and complete internal positions.
prerequisites: Read the linked contract and use the stated runtime, not a planned DAG mapping.
Use deterministic synthetic input and the referenced executable regression case.
tasks: Load the shared two-rust-nodes-distinct-whole-topics fixture and validate its assignment set.
Compare the overlapping-owner and split-topic rejection cases.
Remove one internal position while retaining partitionCount and observe assignment.coverage.
expected: Two nodes may own distinct whole topics for the same admitted fragment.
Each input includes all positions from zero through partitionCount minus one, in order.
Splitting a topic across nodes fails coverage; duplicate whole-topic ownership fails ownership.
Java and Rust validate the same shared cases without providing a Rust numerical runner.
pitfalls: Resolve aliases to authoritative topic identity before interpreting ownership.
Passing offline validation neither authorizes deployment nor fences a live Kafka writer.

lessons.title: Generate mean-reverting demo values
objectives: Recognize the AR(1) mean-reversion recurrence rather than a calibrated continuous-time physical process.
Separate exact noiseless predictions, seed reproducibility and clipping from scientific realism.
prerequisites: Use the module containing the documented Java public entry point.
Keep the recorded synthetic parameters, coordinates and missing-data policy explicit.
tasks: Generate four values with mean 10 and sigma 0.
Set the permitted maximum to 9 and inspect the clipping.
Set sigma to 2 and reversion to 1, repeat seed 7, then compare seed 8 and split-range replay.
expected: The starter values are [10,10,10,10], and clipped values are [9,9,9,9].
With sigma 2 and reversion 1, repeating the seed reproduces values exactly and a tail request agrees with the same whole-range slice.
Episode generation over 601 one-second samples yields chunks of 600 and one, with SYNTHETIC origin and demo fidelity.
pitfalls: The default warm start truncates previous history; general reversion values give approximate, not guaranteed bit-identical, agreement across differently started ranges.
The generator models no balance or coupling to other system signals and is not a continuous deployed processor.

lessons.title: Generate a bounded sine cycle
objectives: Convert period and phase to sample values on an absolute grid.
Distinguish a synthetic bounded run from measured data and continuous processing.
prerequisites: Use the module containing the documented Java public entry point.
Keep the recorded synthetic parameters, coordinates and missing-data policy explicit.
tasks: Generate a noiseless four-second cycle centered at 10 with amplitude 2.
Shift phase by one quarter and predict the shifted samples.
Request the last three starter samples independently and compare them with the original slice.
expected: The starter values are [10,12,10,8,10] within 1e-12.
Phase 0.25 gives [12,10,8,10,12]; the independent tail matches [10,8,10].
The public generator ID set is exactly the IDs covered by the generator lessons.
pitfalls: Phase is a share of a cycle, not radians or seconds.
Noise uses a seeded step-based stream; a bounded demo generator is not a deployed runtime operator.

lessons.title: Inspect legacy real FFT coefficients
objectives: Read all padded real Fourier coefficients and their frequency coordinates.
Distinguish the legacy coefficient API from the browser amplitude spectrum.
prerequisites: Use the module containing the documented Java public entry point.
Keep the recorded synthetic parameters, coordinates and missing-data policy explicit.
tasks: Build the eight-sample impulse at a sampling rate of eight.
Predict eight real coefficients equal to one on frequencies zero through seven.
Replace the impulse by the quarter-cycle sine and inspect why its imaginary spectrum is lost from the returned real values.
expected: Frequency coordinates are [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7], and all eight returned real coefficients equal one within 1e-12.
Conversion copies both coordinate vectors; the original impulse is unchanged.
The real coefficients of [0,1,0,-1,0,1,0,-1] are zero within 1e-12 although the signal has nonzero amplitude.
pitfalls: The result is not a one-sided amplitude spectrum and does not contain the complete complex transform.
Sampling rate is explicit; the direct library call does not perform the Swing dialog validation.

lessons.title: Inspect the legacy surrogate facade
objectives: Inspect the actual implementations behind the two documented surrogate modes.
Test deterministic invariants without claiming seeded random output or preserved Fourier magnitudes.
prerequisites: Use the module containing the documented Java public entry point.
Keep the recorded synthetic parameters, coordinates and missing-data policy explicit.
tasks: Build eight constant samples with noninteger coordinates and value seven.
Call both public mode constants through the facade and verify that removing the constant component produces zeros on sample indices.
Run shuffle mode on a cosine with purely real coefficients and explain why shuffling imaginary components cannot rotate those real coefficients.
expected: Both modes return eight zero values within 1e-12 on coordinates [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7], while the original values remain seven.
Shuffle mode preserves [1,0,-1,0,1,0,-1,0] within 1e-12 because that fixture has zero imaginary Fourier components.
No exact random sample sequence is asserted: this API exposes no seed.
pitfalls: The implementation shuffles imaginary coefficient components or scales complex coefficients, rather than applying an amplitude-preserving random phase rotation.
Math.random and Collections.shuffle provide no seed parameter through this facade; do not teach repeatable arbitrary surrogate values.
